subject: Inference pathway attribution & wiring request
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: sofia.valdez@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 5 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inference pathway attribution & wiring request

Team —

Quick ask from the Acme Health SRE/product folks (looped in): they want us to show a clear mapping from per-route cost/latency signals back to the inference "pathway" (model variant, quantization profile, batching buckets, and cache hit state) so they can understand why a route suddenly spiked in token spend and how SLA fallbacks will behave.

What they specifically asked for:
- Per-route token cost broken down by model variant + quantization profile (p50/p95 token time & cost)
- Cache hit/miss counts at the route level and the contribution to tail latency
- A clear diagram/table describing which fallback sequence will be used when capacity, latency, or cost SLOs are breached (i.e., route -> model variant -> region -> dedicated fallback)
- Ownership: who on the console/observability side owns the telem mapping and who owns runbook edits for SLA fallback rules

I attached a small sample export from Acme (acme_sample_route_export.csv) that has the route names and timestamps they care about. Can we:
1) confirm whether the current telemetry pipeline emits the necessary fields to do this attribution out-of-the-box;
2) draft a proposed UI surface (table + drilldown) and an ownership matrix so we can present to the customer next week;
3) identify any exceptions where automatic attribution will be lossy (e.g., aggregated batching signals that don't include route labels).

Target: sync with Acme next Wed 6/7 to show a mockup. If that’s too soon, tell me earliest possible.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Product — Observability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_sample_route_export.csv

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, sofia.valdez@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 5 Jun 2028 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference pathway attribution & wiring request

Irene — thanks for the clear ask and the export. High level thoughts:

1) Telemetry surface: we already emit model_variant and quant_profile as part of the per-request span, but batching buckets are only present downstream in the serving runtime logs (they're not always joined into the request-level telemetry).

2) Cache signals: KV cache hit metrics are emitted per-device; we currently aggregate them by service shard, not by route. We can produce a per-route join if the route tag is added at the ingress join point — that looks like ~2 engineer-days of work (instrumentation + transform).

3) Fallback wiring: our routing graph is encoded in the routing service (routing rules + policy IDs), but the mapping to the UI is only partially surfaced. We can generate an ordered fallback table if we extract policy IDs and join to the policy config.

Quick clarifying Qs before sizing:
- For the UI mockup, do they expect the primary pivot to be Route -> Model Variant -> Quant? Or do they want Route -> Time window -> Top contributors?
- Is the aim primarily for post-facto forensic analysis or near-real-time alerting? (affects how we design the join and sampling)

Happy to pick up instrumentation scope — suggest we list owners and produce a short spec for Acme. Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Engineering Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

- Customer sync / expectations: irene_choi

I can host a 45-min sync with Acme on Wed 06/07 at 10:30am PT. Agenda: show one-page, instrument gaps, timeline for a staged rollout (forensics first, live diagnostics later).

Attachments: proposal-draft-v1.md

-Kim

Two asks before the sync:
